entity_types.name: Metric
entity_types.definition: A named quantity computed from evaluation results, with a definable numerator and denominator or formula.
boundary_examples: IN: TPR, TNR, Cohen's kappa, recall@5, expected calibration error, pass rate, corrected pass rate
OUT: 'quality' or 'accuracy of the system' used loosely with no formula (not named precisely enough)
OUT: a threshold value such as 0.90 (a number, not a metric)

entity_types.name: Method
entity_types.definition: A named procedure, practice or protocol for building, running or interpreting an evaluation.
boundary_examples: IN: paired eval comparison, open and axial coding, blind relabel, eval-driven development, LLM-as-judge
OUT: a file or dataset the procedure uses (that is an Artifact)
OUT: a software product that implements the procedure (that is a Tool)

entity_types.name: Artifact
entity_types.definition: A named persisted object an evaluation produces or consumes: a dataset, label file, rubric, fixture, record or report.
boundary_examples: IN: golden set, judge fixture, rubric, append-only label file, version stamp, run record
OUT: the procedure that creates it (that is a Method)
OUT: a transient value never written down, such as 'the model's answer'

entity_types.name: FailureMode
entity_types.definition: A named way an evaluation or the system under evaluation goes wrong or misleads.
boundary_examples: IN: eval contamination, position bias, self-preference bias, feature debt, overfitting to the golden set
OUT: a fix for the failure (that is a Method)
OUT: a single observed bug with no general name

entity_types.name: Tool
entity_types.definition: A named software library, service, framework or model used in or evaluated by the work.
boundary_examples: IN: LightGBM, CatBoost, pytest, LangGraph, ADK, Claude Code
OUT: a practice the tool supports (that is a Method)
OUT: a generic category such as 'a vector database' with no named product

entity_types.name: Role
entity_types.definition: A human or agent seat with a stated responsibility in an evaluation.
boundary_examples: IN: annotator, domain expert, judge, reviewer, simulated user
OUT: a named person (not a role)
OUT: a model product named as a product (that is a Tool)

relation_types.name: measures
relation_types.definition: The subject metric quantifies a property of the object.
boundary_examples: IN: (TPR, measures, LLM-as-judge) from 'TPR measures how often the judge passes a true pass'
OUT: a metric merely reported alongside the object, with no claim it quantifies it

relation_types.name: mitigates
relation_types.definition: The subject method reduces the occurrence or impact of the object failure mode.
boundary_examples: IN: (blind relabel, mitigates, self-preference bias)
OUT: a method that only detects or measures the failure without reducing it

relation_types.name: requires
relation_types.definition: The subject method cannot be carried out as described without the object.
boundary_examples: IN: (judge calibration, requires, human labels)
OUT: an object that is helpful or recommended but not stated as necessary

relation_types.name: produces
relation_types.definition: The subject creates the object artifact as an output.
boundary_examples: IN: (annotator, produces, golden set)
OUT: an artifact the subject reads or consumes (that is requires)

relation_types.name: contradicts
relation_types.definition: The text states that the subject method and the object method give conflicting guidance or cannot both hold.
boundary_examples: IN: two practices the page explicitly says are in tension or mutually exclusive
OUT: two methods that are merely different or alternatives

relation_types.name: instance-of
relation_types.definition: The subject is a specific kind or named example of the object, and both have the same entity type.
boundary_examples: IN: (position bias, instance-of, LLM judge bias)
OUT: a part-whole relation (a step of a method is not an instance of it)
